description: Representative Seth Magaziner (RI-02) seeks part-time, paid Summer 2026 interns for his Warwick, Rhode Island office, to start at the middle May until the end of August. Duties include providing a welcoming environment to constituents and visitors, answering incoming calls, sorting and distributing mail, assisting Member and key staff with logistical and administrative duties, receiving and logging constituent input on policy matters, conducting research and drafting correspondence and memoranda, assisting with planning and execution of Member's public outreach at local events, and accompanying district staff to public forums, meetings, and events. Consistent with applicable law, the Office requires all interns to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 as a term and condition of employment.
responsibilities: Provides a welcoming environment and positive first impression of the Member office to constituents, visitors, and other VIPs
Answers incoming calls with poise, professionalism, and promptness
Sorts and distributes mail
Assists Member and key staff (e.g. staff assistant, scheduler, District Director) with logistical and administrative duties
Receives and logs input from constituents on policy matters for the Member office's consideration and response
Conducts research, and drafts correspondence and memoranda
Assists with planning and execution of Member's public outreach at local events
Accompanies district staff to public forums, meetings, and events as a representative to the Member
qualifications: Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Professional demeanor and ability to interact with constituents and VIPs
Organizational skills for sorting mail and managing administrative tasks
Research and writing abilities for drafting correspondence and memoranda
Ability to work as part of a team and accompany staff to public events
Fully vaccinated against COVID-19 as required by the office
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer; we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity or expression, or sexual orientation.

description: Summer internship in Rep. Angie Craig's Washington, D.C. office. The D.C. press internship runs approximately from May 26th, 2026, through Early August, with some room for flexibility. All interns are paid a stipend and provided with the necessary technology for their work. Schedules are flexible to accommodate course schedules and academic programs; however, a minimum availability of 20-25 hours per week is highly preferred. The press intern will have the opportunity to work with staff in both the D.C. and district offices and the program is easily tailored to fit interns' interests and career goals. The press intern will learn about both the legislative process and the communications operation of a congressional office and gain hands-on professional experience while serving the constituents of Minnesota's Second Congressional District.
responsibilities: Work with staff in both the D.C. and district offices over the course of the internship
Learn about the legislative process and the communications operation of a congressional office
Gain hands-on professional experience while serving the constituents of Minnesota's Second Congressional District
qualifications: Passionate about public service
Confident and effective communicators
Proactive problem-solvers
Strong writing and digital skills
Comfortable speaking on the phone and working with the general public
Minimum availability of 20-25 hours per week highly preferred
how_to_apply: Email a combined PDF of your resume, two digital samples and a one-page cover letter to RepCraigPress@mail.house.gov. Format your email subject line as "Craig Press Internship: FirstName LastName." Include your weekly availability between the hours of 9:00am and 6:00pm in your cover letter and confirm that you will be available for in-person work. Applications must be submitted no later than 9am CT/10am ET on Wednesday, April 1st.
equal_opportunity: Rep. Craig's office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age or protected veteran status.

Interns will have a unique opportunity to learn about the legislative process first-hand and the many functions of a Congressional office. The Press and Digital Intern will help build out the Congresswoman's digital and social media presence, with heavy emphasis on creating engaging social media content and graphics.
responsibilities: Help build out the Congresswoman's digital and social media presence
Create engaging social media content and graphics
Answer phones and perform data entry
Assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff
Attend briefings, hearings, and markups
Answer constituent letters on various issues
qualifications: Strong writing, editing, and social media skills to assist with time sensitive assignments
Basic familiarity with graphic design/video editing software
Experience in a press or digital media role (including internships) is preferred but not required
Ties to California's 7th District are preferred but not required

equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.

description: The Committee on House Administration Democratic staff is currently seeking to fill the Communications Intern/Communications Fellow vacancy. The individual in this role will work closely with a fast-paced communications team. Qualified candidates should have demonstrated graphic design experience, strong writing and social media skills, and a desire to help create engaging content. The Committee on House Administration is primarily responsible for oversight of the House offices and legislative branch agencies within the Committee's portfolio. These include the Library of Congress, Smithsonian Institution (including the National Zoo), Chief Administrative Officer, Clerk of the House, Sergeant at Arms, House Inspector General, United States Capitol Police, Government Publishing Office, Architect of the Capitol, Office of Congressional Accessibility Services, and the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights. This is a paid, full-time, limited term position. The intern will learn about House Committee practice, the legislative process, and the policy areas in the Committee's jurisdiction.
responsibilities: Drafting social media content and designing graphics
Editing and captioning videos
Compiling daily press clips
Taking photos during Committee hearings and events
Drafting press releases, media advisories, and weekly reports
qualifications: Demonstrated graphic design experience
Strong writing skills
Strong social media skills
Desire to help create engaging content
how_to_apply: Submit a resume and at least two graphic design and writing samples to resume.chadem@mail.house.gov with the subject line: "Communications Intern _ [First Name] [Last Name]".
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, disability, military status, age, marital status, or parental status. The Committee is committed to, and benefits from, a diverse staff, and candidates of all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

description: The Office of Congressman Salud Carbajal (CA-24) is seeking a highly motivated and creative Digital/Press Intern to assist with a fast-paced communications operation based in his Washington, D.C. office for the Spring 2026 term (late April - July). The Digital/Press Intern will help build out the Congressman's digital and social media footprint, with heavy emphasis on creating engaging social media content and graphics. The intern will work closely with the Communications Director, Digital/Creative Assistant, Legislative Aide/Correspondent, and Scheduler. The internship will run from late April to July, with the possibility of an extended end date. The hours are roughly 32 hours a week and are flexible to accommodate schedules, but generally run 9 AM to 6 PM ET when Congress is in session and 9 AM to 5 PM ET when Congress is out of session. This position is in-person. This is a full-time, limited term position and offers a $1,500 monthly stipend from the office of Congressman Carbajal's unless the intern is already receiving credit/stipend through a third party. Deadline to apply is Friday, April 3, 2026.
responsibilities: Compiling daily press clips
Creating engaging graphics and editing photos
Assisting the Digital/Creative Assistant with social media content, website content and digital newsletters
Clipping, editing, and captioning videos
Assisting with press releases, op-eds, advisories, and other written materials
Creating and maintaining press lists
Compiling regular comms reports on press and social media results

Assisting the Legislative Aide/Correspondent and Scheduler with administrative tasks (e.g. answering phone calls, greeting visitors, etc.) and legislative tasks (e.g. batching incoming messages on Fireside, drafting constituent letters, writing cosponsor recommendations, etc.)
qualifications: Strong writing, editing, and social media skills
Basic familiarity with graphic design/video editing software
Strong social media and graphic design skills
Past experience with Canva, Photoshop, and other digital/graphic/video design platforms is a major plus
Experience in a press or digital media role (including internships) is preferred but not required
California or Central Coast ties and Spanish literacy are a plus
how_to_apply: Interested applicants should email a resume, cover letter, writing sample, two digital samples, and dates/hours of availability to Tommy.Vo@mail.house.gov with the subject line "First Name Last Name – Digital Intern." No phone calls or walk-ins. Deadline to apply is Friday, April 3, 2026. Candidates are encouraged to submit their materials early to ensure timely consideration.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and encourages candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.

description: The Office of Congressman David Scott (GA-13) is hiring interns to work in his Washington, D.C. office for the summer semester. The internship will run approximately from early-mid May 2026, through early August, with some room for flexibility. All interns will have the opportunity to work with the legislative, communications, and operations teams. Responsibilities include but are not limited to answering constituent phone calls, giving tours of the Capitol, attending policy briefings and meetings, researching legislation for the legislative staff, and other duties as necessary. As a result, interns will learn about the legislative process, learn about all the different functions of a congressional office and gain hands-on professional experience while serving the constituents of Georgia's Thirteenth Congressional District. All interns are paid a stipend of $1,200 per month. Applicants who have strong ties to GA-13 are encouraged to apply. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The priority application deadline is Friday, April 2nd at 5 pm EST. Please NO calls or walk-ins.

Comfortable speaking on the phone and working with the public

description: The U.S. House Financial Services Committee – Majority Staff is seeking law clerks for the summer of 2026. The position offers law students the opportunity to gain experience conducting congressional oversight and investigations. Law clerk responsibilities will include conducting legal research, drafting memorandum, letters, and reports, assisting Committee staff in performing administrative duties, and other duties as assigned. Law clerks will work closely with counsels and professional staff on a wide range of issues. This position is unpaid, but law school credit is available. Previous Capitol Hill, prosecutorial, investigative, or litigation experience preferred, but not required. Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to erin.kuhls@mail.house.gov. All applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including marital or parental status), sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, or national origin.

description: The District Office of Representative Joseph Morelle, NY-25 in Rochester, NY, will be accepting applications for an in-person internship during the Summer Semester 2026. Applications will be accepted March 3rd – April 3rd, 2026. Interns will be responsible for completing constituent calls, writing letters, certificates, and proclamations, day-to-day office work, interacting with members of staff in the Rochester office and virtually in the D.C. office, and other duties delegated by members of staff including various constituent case work or work on District-based projects of importance. Interns will learn about the functions of a congressional office, congressional communications, and the legislative process. Ideal candidates should possess excellent communication skills, strong attention to detail, the ability to work in a fast-paced environment, and a good sense of humor. New York State ties are preferred but not required. Internships are intended for current undergraduate students and current graduate students.

description: In the Washington, D.C. office, internships run throughout the year based on the semester calendar. Applicants must be based in Washington, D.C. for the duration of the internship. Interns play an important role in the daily operations of the office and gain firsthand experience in the legislative process. Core responsibilities include greeting guests, answering phones, conducting Capitol tours, supporting the Legislative Correspondent, attending hearings, researching legislation, and assisting with day-to-day office work. Interns may also take on additional duties in Communications, Scheduling, or Correspondence. Full-time paid internships run Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. when Congress is in session, and 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. when not in session. Part-time internships are scheduled to accommodate students' course schedules. Internships are intended for current undergraduate students, current graduate students, and recent college graduates.

Maintain press contact lists and track media inquiries (Communications)
Support logistics for press events and prepare briefing materials for interviews or appearances (Communications)
Assist with processing and tracking incoming invitations to the Member (Scheduling)
Confirm details and logistics for meetings, events, and travel (Scheduling)
Help maintain the Member's calendar and coordinate with district staff as needed (Scheduling)
Prepare briefing materials for scheduled events or meetings (Scheduling)
Support logistics for events, including visitor coordination and follow-up (Scheduling)
Assist with schedule adjustments, conflicts, and communications (Scheduling)
Track and organize inbound constituent correspondence (Correspondence)
Draft responses to constituent letters on legislative issues and policy questions under staff supervision (Correspondence)
Research issues raised by constituents to inform responses (Correspondence)
Assist the Legislative Correspondent in preparing reports summarizing constituent concerns and trends (Correspondence)

Strong attention to detail

Good sense of humor
